title: Soft failover timetables and telemetry-anchored safety net
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: we've observed oscillations during regional overload events where immediate hard cutovers cause cascading circuit flips and noisy telemetry. This PR introduces a configurable 'soft failover timetable' layer that sequences regional failover actions with jittered hold windows, plus a telemetry-anchored safety net that pauses automatic failovers when downstream KV-pressure or egress-saturation metrics exceed configured thresholds. Motivation: reduce noisy reopen/close churn, keep latency SLOs stable during transient capacity shifts, and give ops a predictable ramp for manual interventions. Changeset summary: (1) orchestrator/timetable: new TimetableRunner that applies staged failover actions (drain -> soft-deny -> full-failover) with per-tenant time windows and exponential decay on retries; (2) safety net: telemetry rule engine that samples KV- and egress-related metrics and can temporarily suppress automated transitions when anomalies are detected; (3) grace timers: introduce per-region holdoff and recover-backoff counters persisted to the coordinator store; (4) operator UI: console flags and diagnostic traces for the staged timetable state machine; (5) tests: new unit and integration tests covering jitter, hold windows, and telemetry-triggered suppression; (6) docs: runbook entry and rollout checklist. Rollout plan: deploy as feature-flagged on canary region for 48 hours (canary flag default-off), monitor slo/degradation metrics and circuit-flip rate (alert if flip-rate > 5/min or p95 latency increases > 20%); gradually enable for low-traffic regions then high-traffic. Related: ENG-1189 (design doc), SUP-342 (customer incident postmortem). Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration tests added - [x] feature flag gating - [x] console controls - [x] runbook update - [x] staged rollout plan - [x] post-merge telemetry dashboard created CI/QA notes: integration tests simulate KV pressure and verify suppression logic; we intentionally limited early-time windows to avoid accidental global failover during canary. Merge decision: squash merge after two approvals and green CI.
